about: Bridgit interaction samples: complete request bodies for POST /v1/interactions, one or more per kind, with the reply and the answer each one produces. Source: site-content/content/samples.json plus the card pages in site-content/public/samples/. scripts/samples.mjs builds site-content/public/samples/samples.json, which the app serves at GET /v1/samples.

conventions.create: POST /v1/interactions with the sample's request as the JSON body. Reply 201: {"interaction_id": <number>, "status": "pending", "expires_at": "<ISO-8601>"}.
conventions.wait: GET /v1/interactions/{interaction_id}?wait=55 returns when the owner answers, closes it, or after 55 s (status still pending). The same answer arrives as an interaction.answered event on GET /v1/events.
conventions.answer_question: kind=question: answer = {"button": <button id or null>, "values": {<text or choice control id>: <string>}}.
conventions.answer_html: kind=html: answer = {"button": null, "values": {}, "data": <the value the page passed to Bridget.respond>}.
conventions.resubmission: The owner can reopen an answered card and answer again: a new interaction.answered event with "resubmission": true and "previous_answer".
conventions.html_cards: An html card runs offline: inline CSS and JS only, pictures as data:image/* URLs, no forms, no network. Bridgit.respond(JSON string) answers once (window.Bridget on 1.6.269 and older) (16 KB max). Bridgit then fires bridgit:answered on document (cancelable; detail = {answer, close_after_ms}); calling preventDefault() lets the card show its own confirmation. The card closes about 5 s later. The CARD object at the top of each sample page holds all its text, so a new card is the same page with a different CARD object.
conventions.progress: A single card can't be swiped. Progress through a series is the text "Step n of m" (the pill in these samples), not Stories-style segment bars, which suggest a swipe that does nothing.
conventions.user_visible_tests: Every user-visible test and connection check is a styled kind=html card adapted from the supplied templates; start with html-connection-test for pairing checks. Never send a bare native question as a test; native question samples exist as a fallback and for API compatibility testing only.
conventions.default_card: Default for every owner-facing interaction (tests, connection checks, yes/no, choices, notices, multi-field forms): a styled kind=html card that answers with Bridgit.respond. Start from html-yes-no (decisions, notices: action-card.html), html-choice or html-form (inputs: form-card.html), html-connection-test (tests). Only change the CARD object. Fall back to a native question or notice only when HTML cards are unavailable (older build, an MCP client that cannot show them) or for API compatibility tests; use pieces for live status panels, lists and tables.
conventions.html_answer_values: Forms built from form-card.html answer {"button": "submit" or the secondary button id, "values": {<field id>: value}, ...card.data} inside answer.data.
conventions.html_accessibility: The templates use one column, 16 px text, 52 px touch targets, labelled fieldsets, visible keyboard focus, text alongside colour for errors, aria-live status text and no network or form submission. Keep these when changing a template.

samples.title: HTML card: yes / no question (the default for a simple question)
samples.summary: The default for a yes/no or a two-button decision: a styled card with a large primary button, specific labels and a visible confirmation. Use it instead of a native question.

card.title: Pay the electricity bill?
card.text: EDP, 48.20 EUR, due Friday. Paid from the usual account.

notes: Change pill, icon, title, text and buttons; keep a specific primary label and 2 or 3 buttons at most.
The tapped button id is data.button; anything in card.data comes back beside it.

samples.title: HTML card: notice with one acknowledge button
samples.summary: The default for telling the owner something: the same styled page with a single Got it button. Add a list for steps or details. Use a native notice only as a fallback.

card.title: Your train leaves in 40 minutes
card.text: Platform 4, coach C, seat 21. It's a 12-minute walk from where you are.
card.done_text: Your agent knows you saw it.

notes: Add "speak": true to the request for urgent spoken notices (silent on silent mode). No answer is required: the agent may ignore data.button.

samples.title: HTML card: pick one option
samples.summary: The default for a pick-one question: large tappable options (radio group), a required check and a Send button. The answer is data.values.<field id>.

card.title: Where should we eat tonight?
card.text: Three places near you with a table at 8.

notes: The optional secondary button answers with its own id and no values (here data.button is home); validation applies only to the main button.
2 to 8 options is comfortable; use multi for pick-several.

samples.title: HTML card: multi-field form
samples.summary: The default for several questions at once: pick one, pick several, text, a longer note and a 1-10 slider, with required-field validation, a visible sending state and a confirmation. Values come back in data.values.

card.title: Plan the weekend
card.text: A few answers and I will take care of the rest.

notes: Field types: choice (string), multi (list of strings), text and textarea (string, up to 2000 characters), scale (number). Empty optional fields are left out of values.
Required fields block sending until answered; the owner sees which one and focus moves to it.

samples.title: HTML card: connection test
samples.summary: The default connection check, and the pattern for every user-visible test: a polished card on the shared action-card template. No device action; the owner confirms the answer path.

card.title: We’re connected
card.text: Your agent can reach Bridgit. Tap below to confirm your reply makes it back, too.
card.done_text: Your agent can now confirm that the round trip worked.

notes: Use this HTML template for pairing checks and user-visible connection tests. Change the wording as needed; preserve the styling and response bridge.
Wait for the answer and verify data.button is received before reporting that the answer path passed. Skip is not a passing result.

samples.title: HTML card: demo agenda
samples.summary: The action card page with a numbered list: the demo's opening card.

card.title: 6 things, about 5 minutes
card.text: A quick show of what I can do through your phone. Before each one you can tap Do it or Skip.
list: Front photo: how am I feeling?
card.done_text: The first step is on its way.

samples.title: HTML card: step card
samples.summary: Step pill, icon medallion, info panel, gradient primary button, Skip and End demo, status line.

card.title: Flash the light
card.text: I'll blink your phone's light three times. Look at it.

notes: For another step change pill, icon, title, text and data.step. For a game round, change the buttons too (e.g. shoot / stop).

samples.title: HTML card: photo with a guess
samples.summary: A photo, your guess, optional choice chips and text box, and buttons. Values come back in data.values.

card.title: Did I see that right?
card.text: I think this is a blue mug on a wooden desk.

notes: For a pick-one question set choice, e.g. {"id": "feeling", "label": "How were you really feeling?", "options": ["Happy", "Surprised", "Sleepy", "Something else"]}; the pick arrives as data.values.feeling.

samples.title: HTML card: wrap-up
samples.summary: The action card page as the demo's last card: what happened and what next.

card.title: Want to see more?
card.text: I flashed your light, saw your desk, read your face, came when you said Double, guessed your story and played a game with you.

samples.title: HTML card: checklist and slider mini app
samples.summary: Checkboxes, a 1-10 slider and a send button; the answer is structured data.

card.title: Packing for Lisbon
card.subtitle: Tick what's in the bag already.
card.done_text: Sent. The agent has your list.

samples.title: HTML card: rock paper scissors round
samples.summary: The demo's game page: Ready starts a 3, 2, 1, Shoot! countdown, the agent's hand appears as an icon at Shoot!, and the score and last round sit on top.
notes: The card answers on Ready and keeps counting down; the agent speaks the countdown and takes the photo right after Shoot! (see the demo script, Item 6).

samples.title: Pieces card: live phone status, no HTML
samples.summary: A card made of pieces that Bridgit draws in its own style: a header, metric tiles read from one GET call every 5 minutes, a note and a Refresh button. You write no HTML, CSS or script; loading, stale and error states are automatic. Prefer pieces for status panels, lists, photos and tables; use an html card only when pieces can't draw it.

pieces.text: Your agent keeps this up to date.
Read from the phone every 5 minutes while the card is open.

notes: Sources may name only your own watches and GET calls you are allowed to make (here: the phone module).
The same pieces, sources and buttons are what an applet package's ui.card uses; see https://bridgit.cc/learn/builder/applet-packages.md.

samples.title: Native fallback: yes / no question
samples.summary: One tap answers it. Up to 6 controls; style primary marks the main button. Native fallback: use only when the owner's build lacks HTML cards, an app or tool cannot show them, or you are testing API compatibility.

request.title: Pay the electricity bill?
request.text: EDP, 48.20 EUR, due Friday. Paid from the usual account.

notes: After expires_in_seconds a wait returns status expired, but the owner can still answer late (interaction.answered with "late": true).

samples.title: Native fallback: choice, text box, link and buttons
samples.summary: Every control type in one question: choice (2-8 options), text, link and button. Native fallback: use only when the owner's build lacks HTML cards, an app or tool cannot show them, or you are testing API compatibility.

request.title: Where should we eat tonight?
request.text: Three places near you with a table at 8.

notes: values only holds the fields the owner filled in. Text answers are up to 2,000 characters.

samples.title: Native question with a photo (photo fallback)
samples.summary: image.data_base64 (a JPEG or PNG, up to 2 MB) or image.gallery_id (from GET /v1/image/last). Native fallback: use only when the owner's build lacks HTML cards, an app or tool cannot show them, or you are testing API compatibility.

request.title: Did I see that right?
request.text: I think this is a blue mug on a wooden desk.

notes: Images are for notices and questions; an html card puts its picture in the page as a data:image URL.

samples.title: Native fallback: notice with links, read aloud
samples.summary: One-way message. Only link controls (https:, geo:, tel:, mailto: or an app package). No answer. Native fallback: use only when the owner's build lacks HTML cards, an app or tool cannot show them, or you are testing API compatibility.

request.title: Your train leaves in 40 minutes
request.text: Platform 4, coach C, seat 21. It's a 12-minute walk from where you are.

events: interaction.seen when the owner opens it (GET then shows status seen and seen_at)
notes: priority urgent shows a heads-up; speak reads the title and text aloud (silent when the phone is on silent).
At most 30 notices per hour per agent.

samples.title: Live text panel
samples.summary: A panel that scrolls on the phone as text is streamed into it. No controls, no answer.
events: interaction.dismissed when the owner closes it
notes: Replies are shown for a panel whose interaction_id is 42; interaction_id may be sent as a string or a number. status is pending until the owner opens the panel, then seen.
Up to 16 KB per append; the panel keeps the last 200 KB.
After done: true another append gets 409 {"error":"conflict","message":"This text panel is finished (done was sent); create a new one."}.
